$comment: Routing manifest for the agentic incident loop. An unknown class is notify-only, so promoting a class to agent-actionable is a reviewed one-line data change rather than a code change. See docs/sre/runbooks/agent-incident-loop.md.

app-error-new.why: A Sentry stack trace names a file and line in this repo. This is the class the loop exists for.

post-deploy-synthetics.why: Richest payload we author: deploy SHA plus named failing tests, and it is regression-shaped against a known diff.

synthetics-p0.why: Agent-actionable only for a partial failure. All checks failing means the site is down, which is infrastructure, not code.

app-error-rate.why: A rate spike is not one fixable frame. Correlate and file; do not patch.

smoke-failure.why: monitoring.yml sends only a branch name and a run URL. There is nothing to diagnose until that payload carries the failing check.

canary-gate.why: post-deploy.yml sends no SHA and no test names, so two canary failures are indistinguishable.

deploy-stalled.why: Railway or infrastructure. No code change resolves it.

uptime.why: The site is down. Page a human; do not spend 20 minutes diagnosing.

fast-burn.why: Composite signal already requiring 3+2 consecutive failures. The decision it demands is rollback, which is a human call.

suppressions.$comment: Seeded before Stage 2 so the loop's first act is not fanning out duplicate work on problems already diagnosed. Both fields are required: nothing is muted without an owner and an expiry.
suppressions.why: Monitoring Watchdog / Production Generated Monitoring failures trace to the CSP nonce fix (370edcc4) which is on main but not yet deployed.
